question: Somatic hypermutation is a process that is very important during the immune response because:

options.opa: It facilitates the change of isotype of memory B cells after the primary response.
options.opb: It allows the generation of B lymphocytes with a B cell receptor that will have a different affinity for the same antigen.
options.opc: It induces the proliferation of naive B lymphocytes in the lymph node after the expansion of activated B lymphocytes.
options.opd: It conditions the microenvironment of the germinative center to make the isotype change during the adaptive response.
